neighbours.label: the object noun of a fixed verb-object idiom (pass the time, wet the bed, pick locks, listen to your body)
fire: On long train rides she knits to pass the time until her stop.
Many young kids still wet the bed now and then at night.
The thief had learned to pick locks while he was in prison.
Doctors say athletes should listen to their bodies after a hard race.
Every Sunday evening my son has to take out the trash before dinner.
We played cards in the waiting room just to kill time.
Good teachers find ways of differentiating instruction for each pupil.
After the argument he decided to bury the hatchet with his brother.
quiet: On long train rides she knits a scarf for her younger sister.
Many young kids still need a nightlight in their rooms at night.
The thief had learned several new tricks while he was in prison.
Doctors say athletes should drink plenty of water after a hard race.
Every Sunday evening my son has to finish his homework before dinner.
We played cards in the waiting room with two older strangers.
Good teachers find ways of making lessons interesting for each pupil.
After the argument he decided to call his brother and apologize.
